briefings.headline: Oscar-Winning Songwriter Glen Hansard Dies in Crash at 56
briefings.body: Glen Hansard, the songwriter who won the Academy Award for Best Original Song for his work on the 2007 low-budget musical film Once, was killed in a crash. He was 56.

sources.title: Oscar-winning songwriter Glen Hansard killed in crash

briefings.why_it_matters: Hansard's death marks the loss of one of independent film music's most celebrated voices, whose Oscar win brought global attention to small-budget storytelling.

briefings.headline: Fed Holds Rates Steady Wednesday, But a Hike Remains on the Table
briefings.body: Federal Reserve policymakers met Wednesday to decide on interest rates. The central bank was widely expected to hold rates at their current level. However, officials left open the possibility of a rate increase to address persistent inflation, which has resisted previous policy tightening efforts.

sources.title: The Federal Reserve faces a critical decision on interest rates

briefings.why_it_matters: A rate hike would raise borrowing costs on mortgages, car loans, and credit cards for millions of Americans already strained by elevated prices.

briefings.headline: French Court Ruling Opens New Legal Front Against Oil Companies
briefings.body: A French court ruling expanded the options available for corporate accountability lawsuits against oil companies, setting a precedent that legal observers say may influence similar efforts in the United States and other countries. The decision broadens the legal pathways plaintiffs can use to pursue climate-related claims against energy corporations in French courts, and it signals a growing willingness by judiciary bodies to engage with climate liability arguments at the corporate level.

sources.title: French climate lawsuit offers a window into the next round of the global legal fight

briefings.why_it_matters: The ruling could shape how American courts and legislators respond to the next wave of climate lawsuits targeting major oil companies.

briefings.headline: Fauci Invokes Fifth Amendment, Refuses Senate Committee Questions
briefings.body: Dr. Anthony Fauci invoked the Fifth Amendment and refused to answer questions before a Senate committee. Panel chairman Rand Paul has long accused Fauci of funding research that triggered the Covid pandemic and of lying to Congress about it. Fauci denies both charges.

sources.title: Fauci Invokes the Fifth Amendment, Refusing to Answer Senate Committee Questions

briefings.why_it_matters: The invocation marks a significant escalation in the congressional investigation into the origins of Covid-19 and federal research funding decisions that affected public health policy.

briefings.headline: Upstate New York School Halts AI Humanoid Robot Teacher After Backlash
briefings.body: An upstate New York school district paused plans to deploy a humanoid AI-powered robot in classrooms after state education officials, teachers, and local residents raised concerns. The district had planned to use the humanlike robot as a teaching tool before the objections prompted the halt.

sources.title: New York school pauses plan to deploy humanlike AI robot teacher after backlash

briefings.why_it_matters: The pushback signals that parents, educators, and state officials are drawing early lines around how AI enters their children's classrooms.

briefings.headline: Swift Rescue Mission Crippled After Two of Three Reaction Wheels Fail
briefings.body: A preliminary investigation found that two of Link's three reaction wheels are not operable, leaving the Swift rescue mission severely compromised in orbit. Reaction wheels are critical for controlling a spacecraft's orientation and pointing. With only one of three wheels functioning, the mission faces significant operational constraints that put its primary objectives at risk.

sources.title: Reaction wheel failures leave Swift rescue mission spinning in orbit

briefings.why_it_matters: Reaction wheel failures can render a spacecraft uncontrollable, jeopardizing any mission objectives Link was launched to accomplish.

meta.cold_open: Good morning, it's Wednesday, July 29 — and somewhere in upstate New York, a school is quietly unplugging its AI humanoid robot teacher after parents and students pushed back hard. Elsewhere, we're watching the Fed's next rate move, a landmark French court ruling taking aim at oil companies, and a widening wealth gap between homeowners and renters that's reshaping the American middle class.
